html:
Climate change, in its modern sense, is the warming of the Earth and the changes in weather that come with it, caused mainly by people burning coal, oil and gas since the Industrial Revolution.

Burning fuel and cutting forests release carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases, which trap heat in the atmosphere. The air now holds about half again as much carbon dioxide as before industry, and the world is more than one degree Celsius warmer than in the late 1800s. Scientists linked the gases to warming in the 1800s, and the evidence became overwhelming in the late 1900s.

The effects are uneven:

  • Heat waves, droughts and wildfires grow more common, as in Australia's Black Summer of 2019 and 2020.
  • Warmer air holds more water, so rain can be heavier, as in the European floods of 2021. Storms like Typhoon Haiyan and Cyclone Idai are often discussed in its light.
  • Seas rise as ice melts and water warms. Low atolls such as Tuvalu are at risk, which led to the Falepili Union with Australia.
  • Herders, such as those hit by the Mongolian dzud winters, face harsher swings in weather.

Countries agreed to limit emissions at Kyoto in 1997 and Paris in 2015, but emissions kept rising for years. Young activists such as Greta Thunberg made it a cause of a new generation.
sum: Climate change, in its modern sense, is the warming of the Earth and the changes in weather that come with it, caused mainly by people burning coal, oil and gas since the Industrial Revolution.
